description: The closed failure contract of lux-google-mcp: every code the helper can raise, what it means, whether it is pinned, and how a caller recovers. Generated by reading google_mcp/errors.py and google_mcp/creds.py; tests/test_contract.py fails if this file and the code disagree.
pinned: A pinned code is a refusal a fresh process cannot change by retrying. It is cached together with the identity of the credential bytes that produced it; the next data call re-raises it without a second network refresh. Replacing the credential file, deleting it, or repairing its permissions changes that identity, so the next call re-runs the whole gate (exact scope set, then one refresh, then the identity check) and either succeeds or pins the new refusal. A transient failure is never pinned and is retried on the next call. The serve path never writes a file, refresh included.

codes.meaning: The refreshed credential's verified address differs from LUX_GOOGLE_MCP_ACCOUNT. Neither address is reported.
codes.recoverable: Run `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family> --account <address>` for the configured address, then call again in the same process.

codes.meaning: The selected family has no binding, so no tool can run.
codes.recoverable: A caller error: select one of the families the process was started with.

codes.meaning: LUX_GOOGLE_MCP_TOKEN is unset, or no token file exists at the configured path.
codes.recoverable: Set the variable (fixed for the process lifetime, so a new process is needed) or run `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family>`; a token file that appears at the configured path lifts the pin on the next call.

codes.meaning: authorize would replace a token file that belongs to another account and --replace was not given.
codes.recoverable: authorize only: re-run it with --replace, or authorize the account the file already belongs to.

codes.meaning: The one in-memory refresh failed for a reason other than a refusal (transport, provider, clock).
codes.recoverable: Transient: the next data call attempts a fresh refresh.

codes.meaning: The provider refused the refresh: the grant is revoked or the refresh token is invalid.
codes.recoverable: Run `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family>`; the new token lifts the pin on the next call in the same process.

codes.meaning: The recorded scopes are not exactly this family's read-only scope plus openid and email.
codes.recoverable: Run `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family>`; the replacement lifts the pin on the next call in the same process.

codes.meaning: The token document is empty, torn or not a complete authorized-user document, or the path cannot be opened.
codes.recoverable: Rewrite the document with `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family>`, or repair the file's permissions; either change lifts the pin on the next call.

codes.meaning: The requested tool family does not exist.
codes.recoverable: A caller error: select the family this process serves.

codes.meaning: The base class's own code, used by authorize when the token file could not be written; every other failure is a concrete subclass.
codes.recoverable: authorize only: fix the directory's or the file's permissions or the path, then run authorize again. Nothing is pinned, because authorize is one shot.

codes.meaning: The refresh yielded no id_token, an undecodable one, or claims whose address is not verified, so no read may happen.
codes.recoverable: Run `lux-google-mcp authorize --family <family>`; the new token lifts the pin on the next call.

codes.meaning: A Google API method call failed, so coverage of the answer is unknown.
codes.recoverable: Transient: the next data call retries the provider call.

codes.meaning: The arguments do not satisfy the selected tool's input schema.
codes.recoverable: A caller error: fix the arguments and call again.

codes.meaning: The tool is not in the selected family's catalog.
codes.recoverable: A caller error: call one of the tools `tools/list` returned.
